title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing fairness, starvation prevention, and adaptive timeouts
author: Sofia Martinez
release_notes: Tuned continuous batcher scheduler: improved queueing fairness and starvation prevention; added adaptive per-request timeouts and new metrics. Reduces 95th/99th percentile latency under mixed workloads; config flag `scheduler.adaptive_timeouts` off by default for controlled rollout.
body:
Motivation: The continuous batcher scheduler has been a source of tail-latency variance under mixed short/long sequence workloads. Short requests were observed to be starved when long requests saturated GPU slots. This change tunes the scheduler to improve queueing fairness, add explicit starvation detection, and introduce adaptive timeouts driven by sequence-length and recent service time distributions.

What I changed: Tuning and feature additions are scoped behind a feature flag (scheduler.adaptive_timeouts) and a new fairness policy variant (fairness=weighted_leaky_bucket). Main points: 1) Introduced a per-priority leaky-bucket queue with configurable refill and drain rates to prevent long-request monopolization. 2) Added a starvation detector that promotes requests which have been queued longer than a configurable threshold to a higher effective priority. 3) Adaptive timeout heuristics that compute a per-request scheduling timeout based on recent observed decode times for the request's sequence-length bucket (short/medium/long). 4) Updated scheduling heuristics to prefer batching opportunities while bounding max wait time to meet latency SLOs. 5) Instrumented new metrics and tracing spans for queue_time_by_priority, starvation_count, adaptive_timeout_ms, and scheduler_decision_reason for post-deploy analysis. 6) Added unit and integration tests and a small bench harness to reproduce mixed short/long workload cases.

Behavior and rollout: The feature flag defaults to off. Ops can enable `scheduler.adaptive_timeouts=true` and choose fairness=weighted_leaky_bucket in config to opt into the new behavior. We recommend enabling in canary first and monitoring the new metrics. The change is backward-compatible and can be disabled instantly if regressions are observed.

Benchmarks: On our canary hardware (A100-80GB, 8-instance pool) with a 60/40 short(long-token) mix: 95th latency reduced from 210ms to 160ms (~24% improvement) and 99th from 480ms to 310ms (~35% improvement) when the feature is enabled. Tail throughput remained within 3% of baseline. Detailed bench results attached in repo under perf/bench_continuous_batcher/README.

Testing: Added unit tests for the starvation detector and adaptive timeout computations, integration test that runs the bench harness, and end-to-end smoke tests for scheduler fallbacks and KV-cache interactions. CI covers lint, unit, integration, and perf checks.

Why this is safe: The new behavior is behind a flag and uses conservative defaults. We added regression alerts for quality and latency so we can quickly revert. The scheduler changes do not modify model execution kernels or KV-cache semantics, only the request routing and pre-execution queuing decisions.

Related: ENG-1248 (scheduler fairness project), ENG-1312 (continuous batcher perf epic), SUP-4521 (customer reported tail latency incident).

manual_steps: 1) Enable config flag scheduler.adaptive_timeouts=true in canary cluster; 2) Set fairness=weighted_leaky_bucket and defaults as documented; 3) Monitor new metrics and any model-level decode regressions; 4) If regressions, flip flag to false to revert scheduler behavior instantly.
bench_summary: Mixed short/long workload (60/40) on A100-80GB canary: 95th latency 210ms -> 160ms, 99th 480ms -> 310ms, throughput change: -2.4% (within noise). Bench harness added under perf/bench_continuous_batcher.
changelog_entry: continuous-batcher: scheduler improvements for fairness and starvation prevention (opt-in via scheduler.adaptive_timeouts). Improves tail latency under mixed workloads.
risk_assessment: Low: feature behind flag, conservative timeouts, and promoted requests still honor hard max_wait_time. Monitoring and alerts added. No kernel or KV-cache changes.
backout_plan: Disable scheduler.adaptive_timeouts flag and set fairness=default to revert immediately. Re-deploy previous config if needed.
